content.value_statement: Medical device teams need consistent ISO 14971 risk management across planning, design, verification, and post-market work. This skill helps structure risk files, hazards, controls, and lifecycle reviews.
actual_capabilities: Outlines ISO 14971 risk management planning and file structure.
Guides hazard identification, hazardous situation analysis, and risk estimation.
Applies risk evaluation criteria and risk-benefit review concepts.
Structures risk control selection, implementation, and verification activities.
Connects risk management with software, cybersecurity, human factors, QMS, and post-market processes.
limitations: It provides guidance, not certification or legal advice.
It requires device-specific clinical, technical, and post-market data.
It does not replace qualified regulatory, quality, or clinical review.
Included support files are placeholders and do not provide working automation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Risk Management Plan
use_cases.description: Define scope, responsibilities, acceptability criteria, and lifecycle update rules for a medical device risk file.

use_cases.title: Review Design Hazards
use_cases.description: Identify hardware, software, cybersecurity, and use-related hazards before design verification planning.

use_cases.title: Update Post-Market Risk Evidence
use_cases.description: Connect complaints, surveillance data, CAPA activity, and clinical updates to risk-benefit review.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Risk Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new device project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ISO 14971 risk management plan outline for a [device type]. Include scope, roles, criteria, records, and review cadence.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Hazard List
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate hazard analysis for design input review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a hazard identification table for [device type]. Cover hardware, software, cybersecurity, use error, clinical, and environmental hazards.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Risk Controls
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of proposed controls and verification evidence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these risk controls for [hazardous situation]. Check hierarchy, residual risk, verification evidence, and risk-benefit justification.

prompt_templates.title: Maintain the Risk File
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced lifecycle update after market feedback or design change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the risk management file using these post-market signals: [signals]. Identify affected hazards, controls, residual risks, and required actions.

output_examples.input: A wearable infusion device needs an initial ISO 14971 planning outline.
output_examples.output: A structured plan covering scope, team roles, acceptability criteria, analysis methods, risk file records, review triggers, and post-market feedback loops.

output_examples.input: A software alarm failure may delay therapy interruption detection.
output_examples.output: A risk review linking the hazardous situation to severity, probability inputs, software controls, alarm verification, residual risk, and risk-benefit rationale.

output_examples.input: Complaint trends suggest increased use error during home setup.
output_examples.output: A post-market update plan that reassesses use-related hazards, reviews labeling and training controls, and defines CAPA and risk file updates.

best_practices: Provide device type, intended use, user profile, and use environment before asking for risk outputs.
Supply existing acceptability criteria and scoring scales to keep evaluations consistent.
Use outputs as draft evidence for qualified review, not as final regulatory approval.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for generic risk files without device context or intended use.
Do not accept residual risk decisions without verification evidence and rationale.
Do not treat placeholder scripts or references as completed validated tools.

faq.question: What standard does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on ISO 14971 risk management for medical device lifecycle activities.

faq.question: Can it create a complete risk management file?
faq.answer: It can draft structure and content, but your team must provide evidence and approve records.

faq.question: Does it cover software risk?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes software risk concepts aligned with IEC 62304 integration.

faq.question: Does it support cybersecurity risk work?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes threat modeling, controls, and patient safety impact considerations.

faq.question: Can it replace regulatory consultants?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured guidance and draft content for expert review.

faq.question: What inputs improve results?
faq.answer: Provide device description, hazards, users, environment, risk criteria, controls, and available verification evidence.
